title: Papildu dokumenti (Vestule EKA ENG)
text: Director General of the European Space Agency Dr .  Josef Aschbacher For information: Chair of the ESA Council Juan Carlos Cortés Pulido Riga, No. Re quest to re new the Association Agreement between the European Space Agency and the Government of the Republic of Latvia Dear  Mr.   Aschbacher,  I  have the honour to  refer  to the Association Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Latvia and  the European Space Agency,  signed in Paris on 24 June 2020 by Mr .  Johann-Dietrich Wörner,  then  ESA Director General, and in Riga on 30 June 2020 by Ms .  Ilga  Suplinska ,  then  Minister for Education and Science of the Republic of Latvia . The Agreement  entered into force on 27 July 2020 for a period of seven years  and is therefore due to expire on  26 July 2027. Article  18, paragraph 5,  of  the Association Agreement  provides that it  “may be extended by mutual agreement in writing”.   Extending the duration of the Association Agreement is a sound prospect for further consolidating the Latvian space ecosystem and its further integration into the European and global supply chains. Considering  the importance of this cooperation and the  positive  results achieved  to date , the  Government of the  Republic of Latvia  would be  honoured  if ESA would  give favourable consideration to  extend  the Association Agreement for two consecutive periods of seven years, until 26 July 2041.   Since the Association Agreement entered into force in 2020, cooperation between the Republic of Latvia and ESA has made a significant contribution to the development of Latvia’s space sector. As a relatively new space nation, Latvia particularly values ESA’s support in strengthening national capabilities, developing new expertise and integrating Latvian organisations into the European space ecosystem. Through this cooperation, Latvian companies, research institutions and higher education institutions have developed new technologies, established international partnerships and enhanced their competitiveness in the European space sector. The Government of the Republic of Latvia particularly values ESA’s contribution to developing the next generation of talent and strengthening Latvia’s innovation ecosystem. ESA BIC Latvia was established in 2024 and provides support to start-ups, while the European Space Education Resource Office (ESERO) will be launched in Latvia this autumn, fostering young people’s interest in STEM and space. Latvian higher education institutions have developed new courses related to space technologies, while the National Graduate Trainee Programme offers young Latvian  graduates’  opportunities to gain professional experience at ESA. These achievements demonstrate the long-term value that cooperation with ESA brings to Latvia. A Country Report  on  the cooperation between the Parties under the Association Agreement,  setting out  the  considerations  supporting its extension,  has been  completed and submitted to ESA .   Subject to  the  approval of the  ESA Council,  we understand that  the extension of the Agreement  would  be formalised through an exchange of letters. Yours sincerely,  Ilze  Indriksone Minister of Education and Science on behalf of the  government of the  Republic of Latvia
